abstract: Chagas disease is a vector-borne disease caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi and transmitted by triatomine bugs. The disease is increasingly recognized as an emerging public health threat in the United States (US). Little is known about the Chagas disease system in the Mid-Atlantic US despite the presence of a native T. cruzi vector species, Triatoma sanguisuga. The species is widespread throughout the eastern US, and the Mid-Atlantic comprises the northernmost portion of its geographic range. Triatoma sanguisuga has been implicated in autochthonous T. cruzi transmission to humans in other parts of the US but has never been formally studied in the Mid-Atlantic. To fill this knowledge gap and increase public health preparedness, we investigated T. sanguisuga in Delaware and eastern Maryland. We aimed to collect baseline information about the species, including its habitat, feeding patterns, and T. cruzi infection rates across land use intensities. We collected 151 T. sanguisuga specimens in all three DE counties and two counties in MD, and identified standing dead trees as an important local habitat for the species. Twenty specimens (13.2%) were submitted by community members who had found the bugs in or around human homes and businesses. We detected T. cruzi infection in 23 of 150 (15.3%) specimens and identified 24 vertebrate host species, including humans, from 95 specimens. We detected a stage-structured blood feeding pattern wherein juvenile bugs ("nymphs") were reptile-associated (which are refractory T. cruzi hosts)and adult bugs were mammal-associated (which are competent T. cruzi hosts), which was reflected in a significant difference in T. cruzi infection prevalence between adults and nymphs. Our findings reveal the multiscale network that sustains T. cruzi transmission in Delaware while also providing practical public health information on a local vector-borne disease system.

metadata.title: Ecology of Chagas disease vector Triatoma sanguisuga in Delaware: distribution, habitat, host use and Trypanosoma cruzi infection

summary: Study of Triatoma sanguisuga in Delaware and eastern Maryland: habitat, host use, and 15.3% Trypanosoma cruzi infection, with stage-structured feeding patterns.
title: Ecology of Chagas disease vector Triatoma sanguisuga in Delaware: distribution, habitat, host use and Trypanosoma cruzi infection
